selected_evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared directory with correct ownership/mode (1777)
selected_evidence.summary: mkdir + chown root:root + chmod 1777; stat/ls -ld confirm '1777 root:root /srv/drop' and 'drwxrwxrwt. 2 root root 6 ... /srv/drop'

selected_evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit enforcement) — pre-restart
selected_evidence.summary: dropuserA and dropuserB each created a file; dropuserB's attempt to rm dropuserA's file failed with 'Operation not permitted'; each user successfully deleted their own file

selected_evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before node1 restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 0d6209e2-350d-4cd9-8a7d-11f7c08072be and confirmed /srv/drop mode/ownership (1777 root:root) prior to restart
Backgrounded 'sudo -n systemctl reboot' dispatched and acknowledged locally before the SSH connection was closed by the rebooting host

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node unreachable immediately after reboot (connection timed out), then came back with boot_id 9a507a78-9bd2-4f27-b826-4ee10eaa6366, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and behavior
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart stat/ls -ld shows unchanged '1777 root:root /srv/drop'; repeated cross-user test shows dropuserB still denied deletion of dropuserA's file post-restart, confirming persistence of the sticky-directory configuration

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== creating /srv/drop =="
sudo -n mkdir -p /srv/drop
sudo -n chown root:root /srv/drop
sudo -n chmod 1777 /srv/drop

echo "== verify permissions =="
stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' /srv/drop
ls -ld /srv/drop

echo "== functional test: two distinct users =="
sudo -n useradd -m dropuserA 2>/dev/null || true
sudo -n useradd -m dropuserB 2>/dev/null || true

sudo -n -u dropuserA touch /srv/drop/fileA.txt
sudo -n -u dropuserB touch /srv/drop/fileB.txt
ls -l /srv/drop

echo "-- dropuserB attempts to delete fileA (owned by dropuserA), should fail --"
if sudo -n -u dropuserB rm -f /srv/drop/fileA.txt 2>/tmp/rm_err.log; then
  echo "UNEXPECTED: delete succeeded"
else
  echo "EXPECTED: delete denied"
  cat /tmp/rm_err.log
fi

echo "-- dropuserA can still delete own file --"
sudo -n -u dropuserA rm -f /srv/drop/fileA.txt && echo "dropuserA removed own file OK"

echo "-- cleanup test file B (owner deletes) --"
sudo -n -u dropuserB rm -f /srv/drop/fileB.txt && echo "dropuserB removed own file OK"

ls -la /srv/drop
echo "== done =="
